VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The shared `ProblemDetails.build(...)` helper is the right call and the per-handler messages read well. But this diff introduces a structural inconsistency within the `escalation` package.

**Finding 1 — The new handlers diverge from the established ProblemDetail idiom in the same package.**
The pre-existing ProblemDetail handlers all send the body like this:

- `ValidationExceptionHandler` (line 37): `response.send(ResponseEntity.status(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST).body(detail));`
- `GeneralExceptionHandler` (line 19): same shape, no content type
- `DataIntegrityViolationExceptionHandler` (line 16): same shape, no content type

The 9 handlers in this diff instead add `.contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_PROBLEM_JSON)`. So the package now has two idioms for emitting the identical `ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail>` body, and a maintainer can't tell whether omitting `contentType` on the other three is intentional or an oversight. Pick one convention for the whole package.

**Finding 2 — The content-type/status wrapping belongs in the shared helper, not copied 9 times.**
`ProblemDetails.build` already receives the `HttpStatus` and stamps it onto the `ProblemDetail`, yet each handler re-specifies that same status on `ResponseEntity.status(...)` and now also repeats the `.contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_PROBLEM_JSON)` line. That's the status passed twice and a three-line response-builder duplicated across every handler. Since the helper already owns the "what a problem response looks like" decision, extend it to return the finished response, e.g.:

```java
static ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail> response(Exception ex, HttpStatus status, String detail) {
    ProblemDetail problemDetail = build(ex, status, detail);
    return ResponseEntity.status(status)
            .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_PROBLEM_JSON)
            .body(problemDetail);
}
```

Then each handler collapses to a single `response.send(ProblemDetails.response(ex, HttpStatus.X, "..."));`, the status is named once, and the content-type decision lives in exactly one place. This also resolves Finding 1 cleanly: migrate the three existing handlers to the same helper so every problem+json response in the package is produced identically.
